subject: Unexpected 429s observed — account mapping bug, mitigation and credit offer
messages:
From: Julia Turner <julia.turner@saplinghealth.com>
To: logan.wright@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@saplinghealth.com
Date: 2027-04-27T16:12:00Z
Subject: Repeated 429s from Redwood API since Apr 27

Hi Logan,

We started seeing a surge of 429 responses from the Redwood API around 15:50 UTC today for our production integration (sapling-prod). It's intermittent but affected roughly 25% of requests for a 30 minute window. Our logs show client-side retries but the overall impact is elevated latency and delayed responses to end users.

Can you confirm if there was an operational issue on your side? We rely on the low-latency responses for patient triage flows — this interruption had visible downstream effects.

Attached are a small sample of our request IDs and timestamps. Happy to hop on a call if helpful.

Thanks,
Julia Turner
Director of Integrations
Sapling Health

From: logan.wright@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Repeated 429s from Redwood API since Apr 27

Hi Julia — thank you for the report and the sample request IDs. I'm sorry for the disruption. We're triaging now and I wanted to acknowledge immediately so you know it's being worked.

What we're doing right now:
- Engineering is pulling request traces and rate-limiter metrics for your tenant (sapling-prod).
- We're checking quota mappings and recent config changes that rolled last night.
- I'll follow up within two hours with an initial update; if we need a call we'll propose a 30-minute window.

Short ask from your side: please confirm if any recent plan changes or API key rotations occurred on your end in the past 24 hours. The sample IDs are perfect — thanks.

Again, sincerely sorry. We're treating this as high priority.

— Logan Wright

logan.wright@redwoodinference.com

From: priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
To: logan.wright@redwoodinference.com, Julia Turner <julia.turner@saplinghealth.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com, evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-04-28T03:20:00Z
Subject: Investigating: root cause signal and temporary mitigation applied

Hi all,

Quick engineering update from the infra team: we identified a quota-mapping regression introduced in last night's deployment of the billing/routing service (v3.14.2). Summary of findings:

Root cause (brief)
- A schema change to the rate-plan lookup table caused a small set of newly onboarded API keys to be evaluated against the wrong quota bucket (tenant default instead of project-level override).
- As a result, requests from sapling-prod were charged against a much lower soft limit and hit 429 enforcement earlier than expected.
- This affected ~1.4% of active tenants overall, but Sapling's request pattern (many short concurrent requests) elevated their observed failure rate to ~25% during the window.

What we've done (mitigation)
- Reverted the schema migration for the lookup logic and rolled back the routing change at 02:50 UTC.
- Applied a targeted migration to correct the quota mapping for affected API keys (sapling-prod group).
- Temporarily increased the soft limit for the Sapling tenant to avoid further user-visible 429s while we validate.

Next steps (permanent remediation)
- We'll add a strict unit test and an integration test to catch quota-mapping regressions in the deployment pipeline. (Owner: priyom.das)
- We'll add an audit/CID mapping report to detect early signs of mapping drift (Owner: marcus.lin).
- We'll run a backfill to re-ingest 48h of request accounting so billing and usage metrics reflect corrected mapping (ETA: 48 hours).

Evidence attached: redwood-429-diagnostics-20270427.txt (contains rate-limiter traces and the failing lookup rows).

Apologies for the impact. We're also preparing a customer-facing summary and a goodwill credit to compensate for the disruption.

— Priyom Das
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
priyom.das@redwoodinference.com

From: logan.wright@redwoodinference.com
To: Julia Turner <julia.turner@saplinghealth.com>, procurement@saplinghealth.com
Cc: priyom.das@redwoodinference.com, marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com, evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-04-28T08:10:00Z
Subject: Follow-up: fix applied, proposed next steps and credit offer

Hi Julia — following Priyom's note, wanted to summarize in customer-facing language and list the actions we're taking on our side.

What happened (short)
- A deployment regression caused some Sapling requests to be evaluated against an unintended quota bucket, producing unexpected 429 responses. The issue was isolated to a routing/lookup change and is not related to your API usage.

What we did for you
- Reverted the change and corrected the quota mappings for your API keys at ~02:50 UTC on Apr 28.
- Temporarily raised a soft limit to remove immediate user impact.
- We're reprocessing 48 hours of accounting to ensure usage/billing are accurate.

Customer-facing next steps we propose
- We will complete the backfill and reconciliation within 48 hours and share a usage reconciliation report.
- We propose a goodwill credit equivalent to the higher of: (a) 10% of last month's hosted usage, or (b) the invoiced amount that corresponds to any overage caused by the mapping error. We will finalize the credit after the reconciliation (credit proposal sent as PDF attached).
- We'll share a brief post-incident summary including the tests we'll add to CI.

Please confirm: 1) that our proposed credit approach is acceptable; and 2) whether you'd like a short 20-minute incident review call tomorrow to walk through technical details (we can include Priyom and Marcus).

Thanks again for your patience. We take incidents like this seriously and are prioritizing both technical fixes and minimizing customer impact.

— Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0183
Attachments: sapling-credit-offer-20270428.pdf (PDF)

From: Julia Turner <julia.turner@saplinghealth.com>
To: logan.wright@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@saplinghealth.com
Date: 2027-04-28T09:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: fix applied, proposed next steps and credit offer

Hi Logan — thanks for the clear update and thanks to the engineering team for the quick rollback. The proposed credit sounds fair, and we'd like the reconciliation report once complete.

A couple quick follow-ups:
- Can you confirm the ETA for the backfill completion and whether any usage we see in the interim will be held for manual review?
- We'd appreciate the incident call — tomorrow at 16:00 UTC works for our team. Please send a calendar invite.

Otherwise we're good with the course of action; will await the reconciliation and the credit PDF.

Best,
Julia
Director of Integrations, Sapling Health
